question: With a velocity-aware state, can single-step BC on PushT keypoints recover at least half of the coverage gap between holding still and the demonstrator?

dataset.derivation: tools/pusht_v2/derive.py: x_bar_t = [x_t, (x_t - x_{t-1}) / dt] for observation.state (2 -> 4) and observation.environment_state (16 -> 32), dt = 0.1 s; each episode's first frame dropped

split.source: the pilot's CCIL split (docs/studies/evidence/pusht-m1-pilot/run/labels.json); BC trains on the other 165 episodes

lerobot.plugin: tools/pusht_v2/plugin (lerobot_env_pusht_velocity 1.0.0), installed from the gate's commit

policy.other: every other ACT setting at its LeRobot 0.6.1 default

selection.rule: the saved checkpoint with the lowest mean L2 action error on every frame of the held-out episodes of the derived dataset; ties go to the earlier checkpoint; simulator returns are never used

evaluation.note: the pilot's evaluation through the plugin env, which computes each velocity from the previous observation (0 at a reset, which is at rest)

gate.statistic: the mean over the three seeds of avg_max_reward at each seed's selected checkpoint
gate.rule: pass iff (statistic - hold) / (demonstration_replay - hold) >= 0.5. Pass: freeze v2 and run bc, duplication and ccil. Fail: no CCIL run; try a multimodal single-step learner outside CCIL first
